extra_inputs.what: Calibrated model: per-marker analytical threshold, marker efficiency, noise and stutter parameters, stored as an RDS list. It is fitted beforehand from single-source calibration profiles with inferMarkerEfficiency, getStutterData, inferStutterModel and inferNoiseModel, or with calibrateModel
Population allele-frequency table in the same sequence nomenclature (e.g. the shipped inst/examples/ForenSeq_NIST1036cauc_FWbrack.csv), read with importMPSfreqs()
Reference profile table of the known contributor(s) (refData, read with importMPSsample()), used to condition the hypotheses

runnable_on_strhub_data.why: MPSproto is an R package that interprets MPS-STR (or CE) mixture profiles. It takes per-sample allele/read-count tables whose alleles are in lusSTR's Forward_Strand_Bracketed_form, plus a calibrated model, allele frequencies and reference profiles. It reads no sequencing reads or alignments, and STRhub holds none of these inputs.

notes: There is no executable. The analysis is R code run after library(MPSproto), so program is 'R' and the analysis function stands in as subcommand. The README documents only the interactive GUI: library(MPSproto), then gui(proj) on the shipped example project (README.md:13-20). The scripted workflow (calibration, then inferEvidence under Hp and Hd, then getLR and deconvolve) is in doc/MPSproto_tutorial.Rmd. The recorded command is its main interpretation call, run once per hypothesis (line 182 is the Hd call). Ambiguity: a reader who takes the README alone would record the GUI call as the main invocation. The README's install URL and its project page http://www.euroformix.com/MPSproto both return 404. install_github() needs devtools or remotes, which the README does not name. The Windows zip cannot be used on a Linux runner, so release_binary is not an acceptable method even though a binary is documented. lusSTR (`lusstr strs all` with output_type mpsproto) produces MPSproto's input format. On STRhub data, MPSproto could only be reached through a FASTQ -> STRait Razor -> lusSTR -> MPSproto chain, plus a calibration set and frequencies.
